a1_answer_prerepair_residual:
PROPOSED INDICATOR AND THRESHOLD: Replace the Nyquist-impossible harmonic analysis with a load-normalized top-oil temperature (TOT) residual trend. This leverages the 15-minute sampling interval to isolate the slow thermal drift caused by incipient faults (partial discharge or localized heating) from normal load variations. The indicator is the deviation of the actual TOT from the predicted TOT baseline (adjusted for load current and ambient temperature) over a rolling window. A sustained positive deviation indicates insulation degradation before gas generation peaks.

MECHANISM: Incipient partial discharge (PD) or thermal faults increase local heat generation and reduce oil convective efficiency. This causes the bulk top-oil temperature to rise faster than predicted by standard load and ambient models. Since 15-minute resolution captures sub-hourly thermal dynamics without exceeding the Nyquist limit for low-frequency drift, the temperature residual acts as a leading indicator. This avoids the physical absurdity of detecting micro-amperes of PD current harmonics (0.1% load) via standard CTs, instead relying on the macroscopic thermal signature that accumulates over days.

DEPARTURE FROM STANDARD: Standard DGA relies on quarterly discrete gas sampling; this solution uses continuous online thermal anomaly detection to provide a 30-day warning window, shifting the intervention point from "post-fault gas detection" to "pre-fault thermal isolation."

LABELED PARAMETERS:
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Sampling resolution = 15 min (User Constraint)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Warning lead time = 30 days (User Constraint)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Threshold deviation = +5°C (Design choice to exceed noise floor of typical TOT sensors)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Rolling window = 4 hours (Design choice to smooth transient load spikes while retaining trend visibility)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Baseline model = Linear regression of TOT vs. Load Current & Ambient Temp (Design choice for computability on edge devices)

INDICATOR: Load-normalized top-oil temperature residual (°C)
THRESHOLD: +5°C sustained over 4 hours (ASSUMPTION based on typical sensor noise and fault heat generation margins)

VALIDATION PROTOCOL: 
Temperature: 25°C ambient (standardized test bench condition) 
Duration: 72 hours continuous monitoring 
Sample size: n = 3 independent DEVICES (transformers) 
Data window: 7-day retrospective log per device 
Detection criterion: Flag issued if the load-normalized top-oil temperature residual exceeds +5°C for 4 consecutive hours. The protocol validates the same load-normalized top-oil temperature residual measure declared in the threshold.
